posts.cooked:
I'm just interested to know, how did everybody here first find out about Sentinels and/or Greater than Games?

 

For me, it was when I finally got internet access late 2012, I became a fan of Tom Vasel.  Never knew board games were still being made since the last time I was on the internet was back in 2002 on AOL.  Watched Tom Vasel's top 100 and picked the game I thought looked most intriguing: Sentinels of the Multiverse.  (Big props to Tom Vasel: great reviewer and entertainer).  Ordered it and 2 months later, have got a loyal family of Chicago fans for Sentinels of the Multiverse.

 

Anyone else find out about Sentinels from Tom Vasel?  Or what are your other means?  I'm sure we would all like to hear.

posts.name: Ameena
posts.cooked:
Someone at the gaming club I used to attend had the game, and we played it one time erm...last June or July or so. We played a few games - he had the core set (pre-Enhanced Edition) and Rook City - I don't know if Infernal Relics was even out then. He mentioned that if people wanted to get it, it might be worth waiting till October or so when the new version came out - so a few months later I had a mooch on Games Lore and found it...well, the core (Enhanced) set and Infernal Relics - they were out of stock of Rook City but I kept an eye out and grabbed it a few weeks or so later. From the time I got the game, some time last September, I've played it multiple times nearly every weekend, up till now :D. And of course, I backed the Shattered Timelines Kickstarter and got that when it came out, ordering Unity and Ambuscade as á la carte extras at the same time.

The only things I'm missing are the original four promo cards - Young Legacy, Rook City Wraith, Redeemer Fanatic, and Horus Ra, because they'd already been and gone by the time I looked into getting the game :(.

posts.name: Rabit
posts.cooked:
When it premiered at Gen Con 2011, a friend (arenson9) told me about this guy named Christopher who had this really great game that I'd probably liked. He told me their booth number and I went straight there when the exhibitor hall opened. (Mind you, at the time I was getting to the hall ~8am, so I was one of the first people in when it opened. )

But the booth number was wrong and he hadn't given me their name.

Eventually, I got the rest of the information from arenson9 and got to the booth on Friday. Demoed it and loved it, but mostly I really liked what they were doing as a group and as individuals.

Brought my spouse on Saturday and it was a hit, so we picked it up.  Haven't looked back!

PlatinumWarlock:

I really appreciated their honesty–they didn't try to pressure me to be the older edition, instead encouraging me to wait and pick up the Extended Edition. 

What amazed me was how many people didn't care - they wanted the game right then and bought the older edition, anyway. They sold out of the original edition at Origins that year! It was amazing.

posts.name: Craig
posts.cooked:
I stumbled across the booth at GenCon 2011, after I had purposefully only scheduled myself a couple events. My goal for that year was to play demos and see the new hotness for the year. They were running demo games, so I jumped in for lack of anything else to do.

I thought it looked neat, but it was still on the "eh, maybe list." Christopher's CHA 30, however, had me come check it out again the next day. I realised I was pretty broke at this point, and I wouldn't really be able to afford some of the super chromed-out things I was excited about. $40 was a good price point, so I picked it up.

And then forgot about it after a couple lukewarm games with a friend.

A few months later, I pulled it out for a game night when we wanted something different. And it clicked. Big hit that night, and I've not put it down since.

posts.cooked: I was wandering past a game store in Seatle and saw it in the window.  Checked reviews on my phone, which looked positive, so I figured I'd pick it up when I got home (I was travelling).  When I got home, I discovered that none of the locals had the game and that the Seattle shops probably only had it because they'd physically picked up some copies at PAX, which had been that weekend. posts.name: Ronway
posts.cooked:
I happened to stumble across it while going to a local gaming store. It was right around the time I was really into playing Champions Online, so seeing a Super Hero card game was awesome. However I am a bit of a penny pincher, so I continued to wander around the store a bit, looking at all the other games. However I kept finding myself back at Sentinels of the Multiverse. Shortly before getting ready to leave, I decided to flip a coin to decide the fate of whether or not I should buy it. The coin said to buy it, leading my to play it on a near daily basis ever since.

The best part about it however was, this occured roughly 1-2 weeks prior to its official release at Gencon. Christopher had hand delivered some of the game to local stores sshortly after getting them from the printer. Who knows, if I would have went a few days earlier, I may have bought another game or went gameless. Maybe I would of never gotten SotM at all after that point, how scary would that be?

posts.name: arenson9
posts.cooked:
http://www.spatzel.net/gallery/main.php?g2_itemId=26506 --Young masters Christopher and Paul showed it to me the night before it premiered at GenCon 2011. I'd happened to meet Christopher earlier that year.

 

I was absolutely astounded to hear that they'd made thousands of copies of a game and paid for thier own booth at GenCon. That is a really good way to lose a lot of money. I was anxious that I would have to put on my polite face when they showed it to me. I have played a lot of games and am very picky about what I actually like. Then I played it and was astounded. That first game was a whirlwind. Christopher and Paul were moving lightning fast making tactical decisions as I struggled to even have time to read my own cards, much less anyone else's. Still, I found it thrilling and fantastic.

posts.name: j1hopki1
posts.cooked: I am a game designer and came up with the idea to make a game called Supervillains where each player plays as a supervillain and whoever takes over the world wins. I researched superhero games that were out at the time and found this and a few others. SotM was the best of any of them by far. SotM kind of discouraged me from going farther on my game since I don't think I'd ever be able to create as good a game with as rich a story and with as beautiful art. I have other game designs I'm going to focus on instead. When I find a free moment when I'm not playing SotM, that is.

posts.cooked: My friend and fellow forumite Reckless got me into the game. He had heard about it on the Escapist and ordered it. On the day it arrived, it was the original edition, was the same day he learned that the store where he worked was going to close in about a month or so. My brother who worked at a pizza place got some pizza and we played a game that night with Tempest, Bunker, and Fanatic versus Baron Blade in Megalopolis, and managed to have a pretty good end to what had been a pretty bad day. All of us got hooked on the game and have been getting other people into it ever since.
